In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir of Surah al-Kawthar

It is Meccan.

Al-Mukhtar ibn Falfal narrated from Anas, who said: "While the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was among us one day, he dozed off briefly, then raised his head smiling. I said: 'What made you smile, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'A surah has just been revealed to me,' and he recited: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. ﴿Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar. So pray to your Lord and sacrifice. Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off.﴾ Then he said: 'Do you know what al-Kawthar is?' We said: 'Allah and His Messenger know best.'

He said: 'It is a river my Lord has promised me, with abundant good in it. It is my Basin, which my community will come to on the Day of Resurrection. Its vessels are as numerous as the stars of the sky. A servant from among them will be pulled away, and I will say: "My Lord, he is of my community!" He will say: "You do not know what they innovated after you."'"

Muslim related it from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, from Ali ibn Mushir, from al-Mukhtar ibn Falfal.

As for the words of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar﴾, we have already explained it.

Hammam narrated from Qatadah, from Anas, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "While I was walking in Paradise, suddenly there was a river whose banks were domes of hollow pearls. I said: 'What is this, O Jibril?' He said: 'This is al-Kawthar, which your Lord has given you.' Then the angel struck its clay with his hand, and it was musk, pungent and fragrant."

He (al-Sam'ani) said, may Allah be pleased with him: Abu al-Hasan ibn al-Naqur informed us of this hadith; Abu al-Qasim ibn Hababah informed us; al-Baghawi informed us; Hudbah informed us, from Hammam... the hadith.

Al-Bukhari also related it from Hudbah. Abu Isa (al-Tirmidhi) mentioned it in his book with a narration from Qatadah, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: "While I was walking in Paradise, suddenly a river appeared before me whose banks were domes of pearl. I said to the angel: 'What is this?' He said: 'This is al-Kawthar which Allah has given you.' He said: Then he struck its clay with his hand and extracted musk. Then (the Sidrat al-Muntaha) was raised for me, and I saw near it a great light."

He (al-Tirmidhi) said: This is a hasan sahih hadith. It is also narrated through Muharib ibn Dithar from Abdullah ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: "Al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise, its banks are of gold and its bed is over pearls and rubies, its soil is more fragrant than musk, its water is sweeter than honey and whiter than snow."

He (al-Tirmidhi) said: This is a hasan hadith.

In some tafsir works, with a narration from Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that the Prophet said: "Whoever wishes to hear the rushing of al-Kawthar, let him put his finger in his ear."

This is extremely strange (gharib jiddan).

There is another opinion regarding al-Kawthar: that it means abundant good. It is then a form of fawal from the root "kathrah" (abundance). Allah has given His Messenger Muhammad an abundance of good that cannot be counted or enumerated, in this world and the Hereafter. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: It is the Qur'an. It was also said: It is knowledge and the Qur'an.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 108, verse 2:

And His saying: ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾ means: perform the five daily prayers, and sacrifice the camels. It was also said: pray at Jam' (Muzdalifah), and sacrifice at Mina. This was said by Mujahid and Ata'. And it is reported from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that the meaning of His saying ﴿and sacrifice﴾ is placing the right hand upon the left during the prayer, at the chest (nahr).

It was also said: and sacrifice, and face the qibla with your chest (nahr).

The poet said:

(Abā Ḥakam, are you not the paternal uncle of Mujālid, and the chief of the people of al-Abṭaḥ, the mutanāḥir?)

That is: the one who faces (mutaqābil).

Muqatil ibn Hayyan narrated from al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "When it was revealed to the Prophet ﷺ, ﴿Indeed We have given you al-Kawthar. So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, the Prophet ﷺ said to Jibril, peace be upon him: 'What is this sacrifice (nahirah) which my Lord has commanded me with?' He said: 'It is not a sacrifice, but He commands you that when you begin (tahrramtu) the prayer, you raise your hands when you say the takbir, when you bow, and when you raise your head from bowing, for it is part of our prayer and the prayer of the angels in the seven heavens.'"

And from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi: that a people used to pray and sacrifice for other than Allah, so Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, meaning: make your prayer and your sacrifice for Allah.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 108, verse 3:

And His saying: ﴿Surely the one who hates you, he is the one cut off.﴾ Most of the commentators hold that what is meant by it is al-'As ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi. Whenever the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was mentioned to him, he would say: "Leave his mention, for he is abtar (cut off)," meaning: he has no son, so when he dies his mention will be cut off and you will be rid of him. The Quraysh used to say of someone whose son had died, or who had no son: "abtar."

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Surely the one who hates you, he is the one cut off.﴾ That is, your hater is the one cut off, i.e., the one whose good and whose remembrance are cut off in this world and the Hereafter. Al-batr is al-qat' (severing).

It is also said that the verse was revealed concerning 'Uqba ibn Abi Mu'ayt. And it is said: what is meant by it is Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf. He came to Makkah, and the Quraysh said to him: "What do you say, O rabbi, about this (sunbur)? Is he better, or are we? He has reviled our gods, divided our community, and we are the people of the sacred precinct of Allah, the pilgrims to His House and its custodians." He said: "Rather, you are better than him." So Allah the Exalted revealed concerning him: ﴿Surely the one who hates you, he is the one cut off.﴾
